implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.__init__ creates a 3x3 list (self.grid) and TicTacToeUI builds a 3×3 matrix of Tkinter Buttons.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate placing X and O
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.current_mark starts as "X" and switch_player toggles between "X" and "O"; TicTacToeUI._on_cell_click calls Game.play_turn which uses the current mark.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate moves (inside board and on empty cells)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_valid_move checks bounds and emptiness; Board.make_move only places a mark when the move is valid.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a win and highlight the winning line
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.get_winning_line returns the three cells of a winning line; Game.play_turn sets state to STATE_WON; TicTacToeUI._refresh_board colors those cells with WIN_COLOR.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a draw when the board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full checks every cell; Game.play_turn sets state to STATE_DRAW when the board is full and no winner.
Board.grid stores the marks; Game.scores records wins and draws across rounds.

implemented_requirements.requirement: User‑friendly interface with status messages and scores
implemented_requirements.evidence: TicTacToeUI creates labels for title, scores, and status; _update_status updates them based on Game.state.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Allow starting a new round and resetting scores
implemented_requirements.evidence: TicTacToeUI has New Round and Reset Scores buttons that call Game.reset_game and Game.reset_scores respectively.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Entry point to run the application
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py defines a main() function that creates the Tk root, instantiates TicTacToeUI, and starts mainloop; guarded by if __name__ == "__main__".

judge.summary: The submitted files implement a complete, functional tic‑tac‑toe game with a Tkinter GUI. All core requirements—3x3 board, alternating X/O moves, win/draw detection, move validation, score tracking, and user‑friendly interface—are present and backed by concrete code. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to execute, so the submission meets the benchmark.
